name: Halloween Storms 2003

phenomena.details: X17.2 on October 28 from AR 10486; followed by X10 on Oct 29 and the X28+ on Nov 4.
Multiple fast CMEs: ~2000 km/s on Oct 28, ~2029 km/s on Oct 29. Compound CME arrivals at Earth Oct 29–30.
Dst −383 nT on Oct 30 (main storm). Kp 9.
Multiple major SEP events; GLE #65 (Oct 28) and GLE #66 (Oct 29). Proton flux >10 MeV reached 29,000+ pfu.
X17.2 produced R4 blackout; X28+ on Nov 4 caused R5 (extreme) blackout on the sunlit hemisphere.

impacts.description: ADEOS-2 (Advanced Earth Observing Satellite-2) suffered permanent failure, a loss of approximately $640M. Over 47 satellites reported anomalies. Envisat lost 12 instruments temporarily. MARIE Mars radiation experiment on Mars Odyssey permanently failed.
A 50-minute power outage affected 50,000 customers in Malmö, Sweden on October 30, caused by GIC-induced relay misoperation in the regional power grid.
FAA rerouted flights away from polar routes for multiple days due to HF radio blackouts and elevated radiation; airlines reported increased dose rates at high-altitude routes even at mid-latitudes.
Aurora visible as far south as Florida, Texas, and Mediterranean Europe (~25–30° N) on multiple nights during late October and early November.

papers.title: Interplanetary events and solar wind preconditioning during the October–November 2003 storms
papers.authors: Gopalswamy, N., Yashiro, S., Liu, Y., et al.
papers.keyFinding: Analysed the complex sequence of CMEs and their interactions en route to Earth, showing how CME–CME interaction enhanced the geoeffectiveness of the Halloween storm complex.

papers.title: Energetic particles at high latitudes during the October–November 2003 Halloween events
papers.authors: Lopez, R. E., Wiltberger, M., Elkington, S., Lyon, J. G.
papers.keyFinding: Documented GLEs #65 and #66 during the Halloween storms and the enhanced radiation environment in the magnetosphere.

summary: The October–November 2003 Halloween Storms were a multi-week barrage of extreme solar activity – including X17.2 and X28+ flares, Dst −383 nT, GLE #65 and #66, and 47+ satellite anomalies – representing the most comprehensive space weather event complex of the Space Age.
description: From October 19 through November 4, 2003, active region AR 10486 (the largest sunspot group in over a decade) produced a relentless series of major flares and CMEs near Solar Cycle 23's descending phase. The October 28 X17.2 flare and subsequent ~2000 km/s CME drove a G5 storm on October 30 (Dst −383 nT). The October 29 X10 flare added GLE #66. The November 4 X28+ event (see separate entry) produced the largest known radio blackout in the GOES era. Over 47 satellites suffered anomalies, including the permanent loss of Japan's ADEOS-2 (~$640M). Sweden's Malmö experienced a 50-minute power outage affecting 50,000 customers. The FAA rerouted polar aviation for days. Aurora was visible at 25–30° N latitude on multiple nights. The Halloween Storms became the single most studied space weather event complex and revealed critical gaps in infrastructure protection that have driven policy reforms ever since.
